images.filename: Location Scouting in Rincon de la Vieja (crater-052025-loiacono-3259).jpg
images.caption: Jay Tomlin leads the CRATER team through a section of Rincon de la Vieja National Park, scouting locations to conduct field work. CRATER (Costa Rica Airborne research on foresT Ecosystem Response to volcanic emissions), is a NASA-led project investigating the use of an uncrewed aircraft for volcanic trace gas sampling, in order to better understand the impact of carbon dioxide emissions on vegetation.
images.alt: Jay Tomlin leads the CRATER team through a section of Rincon de la Vieja National Park, scouting locations to conduct field work. CRATER (Costa Rica Airborne research on foresT Ecosystem Response to volcanic emissions), is a NASA-led project investigating the use of an uncrewed aircraft for volcanic trace gas sampling, in order to better understand the impact of carbon dioxide emissions on vegetation.

images.filename: Fisher, Anderson, and Corrales in Rincón de la Vieja (crater-052025-loiacono-4351).jpg
images.caption: CRATER team members (from left) Joshua Fisher, Isaac Anderson and Ernesto Corrales hike through Rincon de la Vieja National Park, Costa Rica, to gather data from trace gas sensors. Fisher and his team placed sensors at locations across the forest to measure emissions, in an effort to understand how vegetation responds to elevated levels of carbon dioxide.
